newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar firms against regionals.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Dollar firms against regionals.

text.p: The greenback maintains its firm tone against most regional currencies at midday on Thursday.
The ringgit was marginally higher on fresh buying against the Singapore dollar but continued strength in the US currency against other major currencies capped gains, dealers said.
"Lots of people are looking to cover their short (dollar) positions because dollar/majors are strong," said the head of dealing at a foreign bank in Malaysia.
He said the market was still thin and choppy as many dealers were still away after the holidays for Chinese Lunar New Year and Moslem Eid al-Fitr festivals.
Dealers said the market would return to normal next week when the ringgit was expected to make fresh gains.
At 0400 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4838/48 a dollar and at 1.7504/7523 a Singapore dollar.
Dealers said technical ringgit buying after 1.7513 level broke had brought down ringgit/Sing further.
Dealers said ringgit was expected to continue appreciating against the Singapore dollar.
The Thai baht slipped below 26.00 to the dollar in early trade after the Bank of Thailand set the midrate at a new six and a half year low of 25.98.
Its bid/offer were at 26.003/010 a dollar at 0400 GMT against 25.990-25.995 on Wednesday.

"There still seems to be bidding interest (for the baht) at the moment. Though it is trading at the top of the range the market appears normal and not overly active," said a Bangkok-based trader at a US bank.
The one month baht/dollar swap premium fell to 11.50/12.50 satangs per dollar against 14.00/15.00 late on Wednesday due to improved liquidity, traders said.
The Indonesian rupiah edged lower against the dollar on the back of relatively ample supply in moderate early trading.
Dealers said anticipation of additional liquidity supply from the central bank on Friday helped ease short-term swaps, which enabled short-term money market rates to decline.
They said overnight money had been kept at relatively expensive levels in the past few days despite sufficient supply due to arbitrage chances between the swap and money markets.
However, dealers said the gap was narrowing after broad anticipation of fresh rupiah supply on Friday after the central bank was forced to support the dollar on Wednesday.
Spot rupiah was at 2,378.50/9.50 at 0400 GMT against an opening of 2,378.0/79.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,376.75/77.50 and 2,376.25/76.75, respectively.
Swap premiums were lower but dealers were cautious on longer-term swaps due to the new reserve requirement rate of five percent which will become effective on April 16.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,377/2,569 and the conversion band to 2,377/2,425 on Wednesday, the first depreciation this week after four points last week.

Singapore dollar held steady against the dollar. The market shrugged off Singapore's finance minister Richard Hu comments that there was no need to take special steps to support the local currency, which had fallen to a six-month low against the US dollar.
The Singapore dollar was at 1.4180/90 to a dollar at 0400 GMT.
-- Madhav Reddy in KL (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Angela Tan in Singapore (65-8703083)
